entries.9b2dbc1def3922024237fd5423ca2996ebcde8e1: <div sID="gen7904" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="25" osisID="1Chr.25" sID="1Chr.25"/> <div eID="gen7904" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7905" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen7906" type="x-p"/> David, having settled the courses of these Levites that were to attend the priests in their ministrations, proceeds, in this chapter, to put those into a method that were appointed to be singers and musicians in the temple. Here is, I. The persons that were to be employed, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.1">ver. 1</reference>), their sons (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.2-1Chr.25.6">ver. 2-6</reference>), and other skilful persons, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.7">ver. 7</reference>. II. The order in which they were to attend determined by lot, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.8-1Chr.25.31">ver. 8-31</reference>.
entries.51c0419abeb35c84ab44512086af5f729889c366: <div eID="gen7906" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen7905" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">The Courses of the Singers. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1015.)</title> <div sID="gen7907" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> Moreover David and the captains of the host separated to the service of the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals: and the number of the workmen according to their service was: <hi type="super">2</hi> Of the sons of Asaph; Zaccur, and Joseph, and Nethaniah, and Asarelah, the sons of Asaph under the hands of Asaph, which prophesied according to the order of the king. <hi type="super">3</hi> Of Jeduthun: the sons of Jeduthun; Gedaliah, and Zeri, and Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the hands of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with a harp, to give thanks and to praise the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> . <hi type="super">4</hi> Of Heman: the sons of Heman; Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, and Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, <hi type="italic">and</hi> Mahazioth: <hi type="super">5</hi> All these <hi type="italic">were</hi> the sons of Heman the king's seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn. And God gave to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters. <hi type="super">6</hi> All these <hi type="italic">were</hi> under the hands of their father for song <hi type="italic">in</hi> the house of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , with cymbals, psalteries, and harps, for the service of the house of God, according to the king's order to Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman. <hi type="super">7</hi> So the number of them, with their brethren that were instructed in the songs of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , <hi type="italic">even</hi> all that were cunning, was two hundred fourscore and eight. <div eID="gen7907" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7908" type="x-p"/> Observe, I. Singing the praises of God is here called <hi type="italic">prophesying</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.1-1Chr.25.3">v. 1-3</reference>), not that all those who were employed in this service were honoured with the visions of God, or could foretel things to come. Heman indeed is said to be the <hi type="italic">king's seer in the words of God</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.5">v. 5</reference>); but the psalms they sang were composed by the prophets, and many of them were prophetical; and the edification of the church was intended in it, as well as the glory of God. In Samuel's time singing the praises of God went by the name of <hi type="italic">prophesying</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Sam.10.5">1 Sam. x. 5</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.19.20">xix. 20</reference>), and perhaps that is intended in what St. Paul calls <hi type="italic">prophesying,</hi> <reference osisRef="1Cor.11.4">1 Cor. xi. 4</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.14.24">xiv. 24</reference>. <div eID="gen7908" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7909" type="x-p"/> II. This is here called a <hi type="italic">service,</hi> and the persons employed in it <hi type="italic">workmen,</hi> <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.1">v. 1</reference>. Not but that it is the greatest liberty and pleasure to be employed in praising God: what is heaven but that? But it intimates that it is our duty to make a business of it, and stir up all that is within us to it; and that, in our present state of corruption and infirmity, it will not be done as it should be done without labour and struggle. We must take pains with our hearts to bring them, and keep them, to this work, and to engage all that is within us. <div eID="gen7909" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7910" type="x-p"/> III. Here were, in compliance with the temper of that dispensation, a great variety of musical instruments used, <hi type="italic">harps, psalteries, cymbals</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.1">v. 1</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.6">6</reference>), and here was one that <hi type="italic">lifted up the horn</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.5">v. 5</reference>), that is, used wind-music. The bringing of such concerts of music into the worship of God now is what none pretend to. But those who use such concerts for their own entertainment should feel themselves obliged to preserve them always free from any thing that savours of immorality or profaneness, by this consideration, that time was when they were sacred; and then <hi type="italic">those</hi> were justly condemned who brought them into common use, <reference osisRef="Amos.6.5">Amos vi. 5</reference>. <hi type="italic">They invented to themselves instruments of music like David.</hi> <div eID="gen7910" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7911" type="x-p"/> IV. The glory and honour of God were principally intended in all this temple-music, whether vocal or instrumental. It was <hi type="italic">to give thanks, and praise the Lord,</hi> that the singers were employed, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.3">v. 3</reference>. It was <hi type="italic">in the songs of the Lord that they were instructed</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.7">v. 7</reference>), that is, <hi type="italic">for songs in the house of the Lord,</hi> <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.6">v. 6</reference>. This agrees with the intention of the perpetuating of psalmody in the gospel-church, which is <hi type="italic">to make melody with the heart,</hi> in conjunction with the voice, <hi type="italic">unto the Lord,</hi> <reference osisRef="Eph.5.19">Eph. v. 19</reference>. <div eID="gen7911" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7912" type="x-p"/> V. The order of the king is likewise taken notice of, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.2">v. 2</reference> and again <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.6">v. 6</reference>. In those matters indeed David acted as a prophet; but his taking care for the due and regular observance of divine institutions, both ancient and modern, is an example to all in authority to use their power for the promoting of religion, and the enforcing of the laws of Christ. Let them thus be <hi type="italic">ministers of God for good.</hi> <div eID="gen7912" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7913" type="x-p"/> VI. The fathers presided in this service, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.1">v. 1</reference>), and the children were <hi type="italic">under the hands of their father,</hi> <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.2-1Chr.25.3">v. 2, 3</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.6">6</reference>. This gives a good example to parents to train up their children, and indeed to all seniors to instruct their juniors in the service of God, and particularly in praising him, than which there is no part of our work more necessary or more worthy to be transmitted to the succeeding generations. It gives also an example to the younger to <hi type="italic">submit themselves to the elder</hi> (whose experience and observation fit them for direction), and, as far as may be, to do what they do <hi type="italic">under their hand.</hi> It is probable that Heman, Asaph, and Jeduthun, were bred up under Samuel, and had their education in the schools of the prophets which he was the founder and president of; then they were pupils, now they came to be masters. Those that would be eminent must begin early, and take time to prepare themselves. This good work of singing God's praises Samuel revived, and set on foot, but lived not to see it brought to the perfection it appears in here. Solomon perfects what David began, so David perfects what Samuel began. Let all, in their day, do what they can for God and his church, though they cannot carry it so far as they would; when they are gone God can out of stones raise up others who shall build upon their foundation and bring forth the top-stone. <div eID="gen7913" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7914" type="x-p"/> VII. There were others also, besides the sons of these three great men, who are called their <hi type="italic">brethren</hi> (probably because they had been wont to join with them in their private concerts), who were <hi type="italic">instructed in the songs of the Lord,</hi> and were cunning or well skilled therein, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.7">v. 7</reference>. They were all Levites and were in number 288. Now, 1. These were a good number, and a competent number to keep up the service in the house of God; for they were all skilful in the work to which they were called. When David the king was so much addicted to divine poesy and music many others, all that had a genius for it, applied their studies and endeavours that way. Those do religion a great deal of good service that bring the exercises of devotion into reputation. 2. Yet these were but a small number in comparison with the 4000 whom David appointed thus to <hi type="italic">praise the Lord,</hi> <reference osisRef="1Chr.23.5">ch. xxiii. 5</reference>. Where were all the rest when only 288, and those but by twelve in a course, were separated to this service? It is probable that all the rest were divided into as many courses, and were to follow as these led. Or, perhaps, these were <hi type="italic">for songs in the house of the Lord</hi> (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.6">v. 6</reference>), with whom any that worshipped in the courts of that house might join; and the rest were disposed of, all the kingdom over, to preside in the country congregations, in this good work: for, though the sacrifices instituted by the hand of Moses might be offered but at one place, the psalms penned by David might be sung every where, <reference osisRef="1Tim.2.8">1 Tim. ii. 8</reference>.

sons, and his brethren, <hi type="italic">were</hi> twelve. <div eID="gen7915" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7916" type="x-p"/> Twenty-four persons are named in the beginning of this chapter as sons of those three great men, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun. Ethan was the third (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.44">ch. vi. 44</reference>), but probably he was dead before the establishment was perfected and Jeduthun came in his room. [Or perhaps Ethan and Jeduthun were two names for the same person.] Of these three Providence so ordered it that Asaph had four sons, Jeduthun six [only five are mentioned <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.3">v. 3</reference>; Shimei, mentioned <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.17">v. 17</reference>, is supposed to have been the sixth], and Heman fourteen, in all twenty-four (who were named, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.2-1Chr.25.4">v. 2-4</reference>), who were all qualified for the service and called to it. But the question was, In what order must they serve? This was determined by lot, to prevent strife for precedency, a sin which most easily besets many that otherwise are good people. <div eID="gen7916" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7917" type="x-p"/> I. The lot was thrown impartially. They were placed in twenty-four companies, twelve in a company, in two rows, twelve companies in a row, and so they cast lots, <hi type="italic">ward against ward,</hi> putting them all upon a level, small and great, teacher and scholar. They did not go according to their age, or according to their standing, or the degrees they had taken in the music-schools; but it was referred to God, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.8">v. 8</reference>. Small and great, teachers and scholars, stand alike before God, who goes not according to our rules of distinction and precedency. See <reference osisRef="Matt.20.23">Matt. xx. 23</reference>. <div eID="gen7917" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7918" type="x-p"/> II. God determined it as he pleased, taking account, it is probable, of the respective merits of the persons, which are of much more importance than seniority of age or priority of birth. Let us compare them with the preceding catalogue and we shall find that, 1. Josephus was the second son of Asaph. 2. Gedaliah the eldest son of Jeduthun. 3. Zaccur the eldest of Asaph. 4. Izri the second of Jeduthun. 5. Nethaniah the third of Asaph. 6. Bukkiah the eldest of Heman. 7. Jesharelah the youngest of Asaph. 8. Jeshaiah the third of Jeduthun. 9. Mattaniah the second of Heman. 10. Shimei the youngest of Jeduthun. 11. Azareel the third of Heman. 12. Hashabiah the fourth of Jeduthun. 13. Shubael the fourth of Heman. 14. Mattithiah the fifth of Jeduthun. 15. Jeremoth the fifth of Heman. 16. Hananiah the sixth of Heman. 17. Joshbekashah the eleventh of Heman. 18. Hanani the seventh of Heman. 19. Mallothi the twelfth of Heman. 20. Eliathah the eighth of Heman. 21. Hothir the thirteenth of Heman. 22. Giddalti the ninth of Heman. 23. Mehazioth the fourteenth of Heman. And, <hi type="italic">lastly,</hi> Romamti-ezer, the tenth of Heman. See how God increased some and preferred the younger before the elder. <div eID="gen7918" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen7919" type="x-p"/> III. Each of these had in his chorus the number of twelve, called <hi type="italic">their sons and their brethren,</hi> because they observed them as sons, and concurred with them as brethren. Probably twelve, some for the voice and others for the instrument, made up the concert. Let us learn with one mind and one mouth to glorify God, and that will be the best concert.  <chapter eID="1Chr.25"/> <div eID="gen7919" type="x-p"/>

entries.e116a5a4de764a43fd7218751bdca9ee396cbd02: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3860"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 25</title> <div sID="gen5542" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.1-1Chr.25.7">1Ch 25:1-7</reference>. Number and Office of the Singers.<div eID="gen5542" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5543" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3860"/><hi type="bold">1. David and the captains of the host--</hi>that is, the princes (<reference osisRef="1Chr.23.2">1Ch 23:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Chr.24.6">24:6</reference>). It is probable that the king was attended on the occasion of arranging the singers by the same parties that are mentioned as having assisted him in regulating the order of the priests and Levites. <div eID="gen5543" type="x-p"/>
entries.5d481a46e444c22327679a78e78c20b9d59dbdd1: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3861"/><div sID="gen5544" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3861"/><hi type="bold">2. according to the order of the king--</hi>Hebrew, "by the hands of the king," that is, "according to the king's order," under the personal superintendence of Asaph and his colleagues.<div eID="gen5544" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5545" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">which prophesied--</hi>that is, in this connection, played with instruments. This metaphorical application of the term "prophecy" most probably originated in the practice of the prophets, who endeavored to rouse their prophetic spirit by the animating influence of music (see on <reference osisRef="2Kgs.3.15">2Ki 3:15</reference>). It is said that Asaph did this "according to David's order," because by royal appointment he officiated in the tabernacle on Zion (<reference osisRef="1Chr.16.37-1Chr.16.41">1Ch 16:37-41</reference>), while other leaders of the sacred music were stationed at Gibeon. <div eID="gen5545" type="x-p"/>
entries.008caa0222bdcff0b46ca95feced05b503dc2aa8: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3862"/><div sID="gen5546" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3862"/><hi type="bold">5. Heman the king's seer--</hi>The title of "seer" or "prophet of David" is also given to Gad (<reference osisRef="1Chr.21.9">1Ch 21:9</reference>), and to Jeduthun (<reference osisRef="2Chr.29.14">2Ch 29:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Chr.29.15">15</reference>), in the words (Margin, "matters") of God.<div eID="gen5546" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5547" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to lift up the horn--</hi>that is, to blow loudly in the worship of God; or perhaps it means nothing more than that he presided over the wind instruments, as Jeduthun over the harp. Heman had been appointed at first to serve at Gibeon (<reference osisRef="1Chr.16.41">1Ch 16:41</reference>). But his destination seems to have been changed at a subsequent period.<div eID="gen5547" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5548" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">God gave to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters--</hi>The daughters are mentioned, solely because from their musical taste and talents they formed part of the choir (<reference osisRef="Ps.68.25">Psa 68:25</reference>). <div eID="gen5548" type="x-p"/>
entries.c9516b562b62c0ad1c56f699b9c40245ef64d93d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3863"/><div sID="gen5549" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3863"/><hi type="bold">6-7. All these were under the hands of their father--</hi>Asaph had four sons, Jeduthun six, and Heman fourteen, equal to twenty-four; making the musicians with their brethren the singers, an amount of two hundred eighty-eight. For, like the priests and Levites, they were divided into twenty-four courses of twelve men each, equal to two hundred eighty-eight, who served a week in rotation; and these, half of whom officiated every week with a proportionate number of assistants, were skilful and experienced musicians, capable of leading and instructing the general musical corps, which comprised no less than four thousand (<reference osisRef="1Chr.23.5">1Ch 23:5</reference>).<div eID="gen5549" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5550" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.8-1Chr.25.31">1Ch 25:8-31</reference>. Their Division by Lot into Four and Twenty Orders. <div eID="gen5550" type="x-p"/>
entries.c0e5e52c0494d26cedddf1783bf10a180da7d5e2: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv3864"/><div sID="gen5551" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv3864"/><hi type="bold">8. they cast lots, ward against ward--</hi>"Ward" is an old English word for "division" or "company." The lot was cast to determine the precedence of the classes or divisions over which the musical leaders presided; and, in order to secure an impartial arrangement of their order, the master and his assistants, the teacher and his scholars, in each class or company took part in this solemn casting of lots. In the first catalogue given in this chapter the courses are classed according to their employment as musicians. In the second, they are arranged in the order of their service. <chapter eID="1Chr.25"/>

entries.ec6f87cd37b51997380c5f527d198a164eeb1806: <div eID="gen13795" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen13796" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen13797" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen13797" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen13796" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen13798" type="x-p"/> The number and offices of the singers and players on musical instruments; and their division by lot into twenty-four courses, vv. 1-31. <div eID="gen13798" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13799" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen13799" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13800" type="x-p"/> David and the captains of the host - The chiefs of those who formed the several orders: not military captains. <div eID="gen13800" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13801" type="x-p"/> Should prophesy - Should accompany their musical instruments with prayer and singing.
entries.f4daada1b75d35bcab48bf7c4b663655facf1c9d: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen13801" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13802" type="x-p"/> Which prophesied - Sung hymns and prayed. But the Targum understands this of prophesying in the proper sense of the term; and therefore says, "Who prophesied by the Holy Spirit." Jarchi is of the same opinion and quotes the case of Elisha, <reference osisRef="2Kgs.3.15">2Kgs 3:15</reference>; While the minstrel played, the hand of the Lord [i.e., the spirit of prophecy] was upon him.
entries.7c35c32db26def5bd29884ff0debce83c4f7be45: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen13802" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13803" type="x-p"/> The sons of Jeduthun - six - That is, six with their father, otherwise, there are but five. Hence it is said, they were under the hands of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with a harp, etc.
entries.028daefd176518d3611be8de977b845b25633f0a: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen13803" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13804" type="x-p"/> To lift up the horn - "The horn of prophecy," says Jarchi; "to sound with the trumpet in the words of prophecy before the Lord." - T. <div eID="gen13804" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13805" type="x-p"/> Three daughters - These also were employed among the singers.
entries.88e1de14356a2318ff8c940bd43a6a25d97ce4d9: <hi type="bold">Verse 7</hi> <div eID="gen13805" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13806" type="x-p"/> Two hundred fourscore and eight - That it twelve classes of twenty-four Levites each; for two hundred and eighty-eight divided by twelve quotes twenty-four.
entries.7c0f5714ab3090f214e09cbfe4da636486b54337: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen13806" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13807" type="x-p"/> For Asaph to Joseph - His first-born. <div eID="gen13807" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13808" type="x-p"/> The second to Gedaliah - The first-born of Jeduthun.
entries.a024c8c6de2027d1846df3f5ce6cb4e784b55614: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen13808" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13809" type="x-p"/> The third to Zaccur - The first-born of Asaph.
entries.3df917c8434cfd1602915b60a2d3f845d42b4cb7: <hi type="bold">Verse 11</hi> <div eID="gen13809" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13810" type="x-p"/> The fourth to Izri - The second son of Jeduthun.
entries.9b007ad05cdb0eb661e5cd93ad3c7749f0d33b2e: <hi type="bold">Verse 12</hi> <div eID="gen13810" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13811" type="x-p"/> The fifth to Nethaniah - The third son of Asaph. Thus we find the lot did not run in any particular kind of order.
entries.49e92b3237d6b55a66a27cdd89e21bbc89d77834: <hi type="bold">Verse 14</hi> <div eID="gen13811" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13812" type="x-p"/> Jesharelah - Supposed to be the same with Uzziel, son of Heman.
entries.a3510e20c9d3b641694b0ddec3e2a100d205ce31: <hi type="bold">Verse 31</hi> <div eID="gen13812" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13813" type="x-p"/> Romamti-ezer - Both these names belong to the same person. He is mentioned also <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.4">1Chr 25:4</reference>. <div eID="gen13813" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13814" type="x-p"/> With this immense parade of noise and show, (David's own invention), Christianity has nothing to do.  <chapter eID="1Chr.25"/> <div eID="gen13814" type="x-p"/>

entries.5bd3f5cfa1d9239ceaafa557925fd5bec5f439a4: <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.1">1Ch 25:1</reference> <hi type="italic">The twenty-four classes of musicians</hi>. - 1Ch 25:1. “David and the princes of the host separated for the service the sons of Asaph,” etc. הצּבא שׂרי are not princes of the Levite host; for although the service of the Levites is called צבא צבא in Num 4:23, yet the princes of the Levites are nowhere called הצבא שׂרי. This expression rather denotes either the leaders of the army of the chiefs of Israel, as the host of Jahve, <reference osisRef="Exod.12.17">Exo 12:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.12.41">Exo 12:41</reference>, etc. Here it is used in the last signification, as synonymous with princes of Israel (<reference osisRef="1Chr.23.2">1Ch 23:2</reference>); in <reference osisRef="Exod.24.6">Exo 24:6</reference> we have simply the princes, along with whom the heads of the fathers'-houses of the priests and the Levites are mentioned. לעבדה הבדּיל, separate for the service; cf. Num 16:9. The ל in אסף לבני is <hi type="italic">nota acc</hi>. Since Asaph was, according to <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.39-1Chr.6.43">1Ch 6:39-43</reference>, a descendant of Gershon, Heman, according to <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.33-1Chr.6.38">1Ch 6:33-38</reference>, a descendant of Kohath, and Jeduthun (= Ethan) a descendant of Merari (<reference osisRef="1Chr.6.44-1Chr.6.47">1Ch 6:44-47</reference>), all the chief families of Levi had representatives among the singers. The Kethibh הנביאים is an orthographical error for הנּבּאים (<hi type="italic">Keri</hi>), partic. Niph., corresponding to the singular הנּבּא, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.2">1Ch 25:2</reference> and 1Ch 25:3. נּבּא, <hi type="italic">prophetare</hi>, is here used in its wider signification of the singing and playing to the praise of God performed in the power of the Divine Spirit. In reference to the instruments of these chief musicians, cf. 1Ch 15:16. The suffix in מספּרם refers to the following noun, which is subordinated to the word מספּר as genitive; cf. the similar construction עצל נפשׁו, his, the sluggard’s, soul, <reference osisRef="Prov.13.4">Pro 13:4</reference>, and Ew. §309, <hi type="italic">e</hi>. “Their number (the number) of the workmen for the service, i.e., of those who performed the work of the service, was (as follows).”
entries.dde7481883b5773641d8cbc49e2a7e65e4d733f8: <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.2-1Chr.25.3">1Ch 25:2-3</reference> <div eID="gen5846" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5847" type="x-p"/> With אסף לבני the enumeration beings: “Of Asaph’s sons were, or to Asaph’s sons belonged, Zacchur,” etc. Four are here named, but the number is not stated, while it is given in the case of the sons of Jeduthun and Heman, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.3">1Ch 25:3</reference> and 1Ch 25:5. על־יד, at the hand, alternates with על־ידי (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.3">1Ch 25:3</reference> and <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.6">1Ch 25:6</reference>), and אסף יד על does not of itself express a different relationship to Asaph than that expressed by המּלך ידי על with reference to the king. It signifies only “under (according to) the direction of;” and in <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.6">1Ch 25:6</reference> the king, Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman are co-ordinated, inasmuch as the musical part of the worship was arranged by David and the three chief musicians in common, although only the latter were concerned in its performance. In <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.3">1Ch 25:3</reference> לידוּתוּן is placed at the beginning, because the choir of singers led by him bore his name; and so also in the case of Heman, 1Ch 25:4. “As to Jeduthun, were sons of Jeduthun.” The word sons in these catalogues denotes not merely actual sons, but those intellectually sons, i.e., scholars taught by the master. This is clear from the fact that the twenty-four classes, each of which numbered twelve men, consist of sons and brothers of the leaders. The names given as those of the sons of Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman, in <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.2-1Chr.25.5">1Ch 25:2-5</reference>, do not represent the whole number of the scholars of these masters, but only the presidents of the twenty-four classes of Levites who were engaged under their leadership in performing the sacred music. Only five sons of Jeduthun are named in our text, while according to the number given there should be six. A comparison of the names in vv. 9-31 shows that in <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.3">1Ch 25:3</reference> the name שׁמעי (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.17">1Ch 25:17</reference>) has been dropped out. בּכּנּור belongs to ידוּתוּן: under the direction of their father Jeduthun (the master), upon the kinnor (see on <reference osisRef="1Chr.15.16">1Ch 15:16</reference>), who was inspired to sing praise, i.e., who played inspiredly to bring praise and honour to the Lord; cf. <reference osisRef="1Chr.16.4">1Ch 16:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Chr.23.30">1Ch 23:30</reference>, etc.
entries.1e85c83eccc111689d216ea0e652f576f338343e: <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.4-1Chr.25.5">1Ch 25:4-5</reference> <div eID="gen5847" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5848" type="x-p"/> Fourteen sons of Heman are enumerated. עזר רממתּי is one name, cf. 31, although עזר is without doubt to be supplied also after גּדּלתּי. Probably also מחזיאות is to be supplied in thought after the names. מלותי, I made full, and הותיר, increased. (Note: On these names Ewald ways, <hi type="italic">ausf. Lehrb. der Hebr. Sprache,</hi> §274, S. 672, der 7 Ausg.: “It is thought that the utterance of a great prophet is to be found cut up into names of near relatives, when the words, עזר רממתּי גּדּלתּי מחזיאות הותיר מלותי 'I have given great and lofty help, <div eID="gen5848" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5849" type="x-p"/> I have to fulness spoken oracles,' which manifestly form a verse, and may have been the commencement of a famed ancient oracle, are found transferred to the five musical sons of Heman, Giddalti(ezer), Romamtiezer, Mallothi, Hothir, and Machazioth.”) <div eID="gen5849" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5850" type="x-p"/> Heman is called in <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.5">1Ch 25:5</reference> the seer of the king in the words of God, because he, along with his gift of song, was endowed also with the prophetic gift, and as seer made known to the king revelations of God. In <reference osisRef="2Chr.35.15">2Ch 35:15</reference> the same thing is predicated also of Jeduthun, and in the same sense the prophet Gad is called in <reference osisRef="1Chr.21.9">1Ch 21:9</reference> David’s seer. קרן להרים the Masoretes have connected with the preceding, by placing Athnach under the קרן, and the phrase has been wholly misunderstood by the Rabbins and Christian commentators. Berth., e.g., connects it with האלהים בּדברי, and translates, “to sound loud upon horns, according to the divine command,” referring to <reference osisRef="2Chr.29.15">2Ch 29:15</reference>, where, however, both meaning and accentuation forbid us to connect יהוה בּדברי with what follows. This interpretation of the words is thoroughly wrong, not only because the Levites under Heman’s direction did not blow horns, the horn not being one of the instruments played by the Levites in connection with the worship, but also because on linguistic grounds it is objectionable. קרן הרים קרן .el never has the signification to blow the horn; for to elevate the horn signifies everywhere to heighten the power of any one, or unfold, show power; cf. <reference osisRef="1Sam.2.10">1Sa 2:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lam.2.17">Lam 2:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.148.14">Psa 148:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.89.18">Psa 89:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.92.11">Psa 92:11</reference>, etc. That is the meaning of the phrase here, and the words are to be connected, according to their sense, with what follows: “to elevate the horn,” i.e., to give power, God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters; i.e., to make Heman’s race mighty for the praise of God, God gave him so many sons and daughters.
entries.6ca4053798b9818e713010c54142b83004957caa: <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.6-1Chr.25.7">1Ch 25:6-7</reference> <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.6">1Ch 25:6</reference> is the subscription to the enumeration, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.2">1Ch 25:2</reference>-5. כּל־אלּה are not the fourteen sons of Heman, but all the sons of Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman. All these were under the direction of their fathers for song in the house of Jahve, with cymbals ... for the service in the house of God under the direction of the king, etc. אביהם is used distributively of each father of the sons named. Bertheau supplies after אביהם the name Heman, and thereby the first half of the verse contradicts the second, which he correctly understands to refer to the twenty-four persons enumerated. - In <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.7">1Ch 25:7</reference> the total number is given. Their number (the number) of the sons of Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman (i.e., of the twenty-four 4 + 6 + 14 mentioned by name), with their brethren, was 288 (24 x 12); whence we learn that each of those named had eleven אחים, all of them שׁיר מלמּדי שׁיר, learned, practised in song for Jahve. In כּל־המּבין the sons and the brothers are both included, in order to give the total number. מבין, having understanding, knowledge of a thing, denotes here those who by education and practice were skilled in song - the accomplished musicians. Their number was 288, and these were divided into twenty-four choirs (classes). David had, according to <reference osisRef="1Chr.23.5">1Ch 23:5</reference>, appointed 4000 Levites for the performance of the music. Of these, 288 were מבינים skilled in song; the others were scholars (תּלמידים), as <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.8">1Ch 25:8</reference> shows, where מבין and תּלמיד are the two categories into which the musicians are divided.
entries.8acdd289eac08fa978ba86c9da43007f8afcc2ca: <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.8">1Ch 25:8</reference> <div eID="gen5850" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5851" type="x-p"/> They cast lots, משׁמרת גּורלות, κλήρους ἐφημερίων (lxx), by which the משׁמרת, the waiting upon the service, was fixed, that is, the order of their succession in the official service. לעמּת is variously translated. As no name follows, R. Shel. and Kimchi would repeat the preceding משׁמרת: one class as the other; and this is supported by <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.16">1Ch 26:16</reference> and <reference osisRef="Neh.12.24">Neh 12:24</reference>, and by the fact that in <reference osisRef="1Chr.17.5">1Ch 17:5</reference>, after ממּשׁכּן, the words משׁכּן אל have been dropped out. But according to the accentuation משׁמרת belongs to גּורלות, and so the proposed completion is at once disposed of. Besides this, however, the thought “class like class” does not appear quite suitable, as the classes were only formed by the lots, and so were not in existence so as to be able to cast lots. We therefore, with Ewald, §360, <hi type="italic">a</hi>, and Berth., hold the clause כּגּדול כּקּטן to be the genitive belonging to לעמּת, since עמּת is in <reference osisRef="Eccl.5.15">Ecc 5:15</reference> also connected with a clause: “in the manner of, as the small, so the great,” i.e., the small and the great, the older as the younger. This is further defined by “the skilled as the scholars.” From these words it is manifest that not merely the 288 cast lots, for these were כּל־מבין (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.7">1Ch 25:7</reference>), but also the other 3712 Levites appointed for the service of the singers; whence it further follows that only the 288 who were divided by lot into twenty-four classes, each numbering twelve persons, were thoroughly skilled in singing and playing, and the scholars were so distributed to them that each class received an equal number of them, whom they had to educate and train. These, then, were probably trained up for and employed in the temple music according to their progress in their education, so that the ἐφημερία which had at any time charge of the service consisted not only of the twelve skilled musicians, but also of a number of scholars who assisted in singing and playing under their direction.
entries.2d0bdcb1809e14bdaeeb51db400cb5b9dd258428: <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.9-1Chr.25.31">1Ch 25:9-31</reference> <div eID="gen5851" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5852" type="x-p"/> The order of succession was so determined by lot, that the four sons of Asaph (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.3">1Ch 25:3</reference>) received the first, third, fifth, and seventh places; the six sons of Jeduthun, the second, fourth, eighth, twelfth, and fourteenth; and finally, the four sons of Heman (first mentioned in <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.4">1Ch 25:4</reference>), the sixth, ninth, eleventh, and thirteenth places; while the remaining places, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.15-1Chr.25.24">1Ch 25:15-24</reference>, fell to the other sons of Heman. From this we learn that the lots of the sons of the three chief musicians were not placed in separate urns, and one lot drawn from each alternately; but that, on the contrary, all the lots were placed in one urn, and in drawing the lots of Asaph and Jeduthun came out so, that after the fourteenth drawing only sons of Heman remained.<note placement="foot">Bertheau, S. 218, draws quite another conclusion from the above-mentioned order in which the lots were drawn. He supposes “that two series, each of seven, were first included in the lot: to the one series belonged the four sons of Asaph and the three sons of Heman, Mattaniah, Uzziel or Azarel, and Shebuel or Shubael; to the other, the six sons of Jeduthun and Bukkiah the son of Heman. A lot was drawn from each series alternately, commencing with the first, so that the four sons of Asaph and the three sons of Heman obtained the places 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13; while to the six sons of Jeduthun, and the son of Heman added to them, fell the places 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. The still remaining ten sons of Heman were then finally drawn for, and received the placed from the 15th to the 24th.” This very artificial hypothesis explains, indeed, the order of the lots, but we cannot think it probable, because (1) for the supposed dividing of the lots to be drawn into divisions of 10 and 14 no reason can be assigned; (2) by any such division the sons of Heman would have been placed at a disadvantage from the beginning as compared with the sons of Asaph and Jeduthun, since not only Asaph’s four sons, but also all Jeduthun’s six sons, would have been placed in the first rank, while only four sons of Heman accompany them, Heman’s ten remaining sons having had the last place assigned them.</note> <div eID="gen5852" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5853" type="x-p"/> As to the details in <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.9">1Ch 25:9</reference>, after Joseph we miss the statement, “he and his sons and his brothers, twelve;” which, with the exception of the הוּא, used only of the second lot, and omitted for the sake of brevity in all the other cases, is repeated with all the 23 numbers, and so can have been dropped here only by an error. The words ליוסף לאסף are to be understood thus: The first lot drawn was for Asaph, viz., for his son Joseph. In the succeeding verses the names are enumerated, sometimes with and sometimes without ל. Some of the names diverge somewhat in form. Izri, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.11">1Ch 25:11</reference>, stands for Zeri, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.3">1Ch 25:3</reference>; Jesharelah, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.14">1Ch 25:14</reference>, for Asarelah, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.2">1Ch 25:2</reference>; Azarel, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.18">1Ch 25:18</reference>, for Uzziel, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.4">1Ch 25:4</reference> (like the king’s names Uzziah and Azariah, <reference osisRef="1Chr.3.12">1Ch 3:12</reference>, and <reference osisRef="2Chr.26.1">2Ch 26:1</reference>); Shubael, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.20">1Ch 25:20</reference>, for Shebuel, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.4">1Ch 25:4</reference> (cf. <reference osisRef="1Chr.23.16">1Ch 23:16</reference> with <reference osisRef="1Chr.24.20">1Ch 24:20</reference>); Jeremoth, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.22">1Ch 25:22</reference>, for Jerimoth, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.4">1Ch 25:4</reference>; Eliyathah, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.27">1Ch 25:27</reference>, for Eliathah, 1Ch 25:4. Besides these, the fuller forms Nethanyahu (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.12">1Ch 25:12</reference>), Hashabyahu (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.3">1Ch 25:3</reference>), Hananyahu (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.23">1Ch 25:23</reference>), are used instead of the shorter Nethaniah, etc. (<reference osisRef="1Chr.25.2">1Ch 25:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.19">1Ch 25:19</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.4">1Ch 25:4</reference>). Of the 24 names which are here enumerated, besides those of Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman, only Mattithiah recurs (<reference osisRef="1Chr.15.18">1Ch 15:18</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.15.21">1Ch 15:21</reference>) in the description of the solemnities connected with the bringing in of the ark; “but we are not justified in seeking there the names of our twenty-four classes” (Berth.).  <chapter eID="1Chr.25"/> <div eID="gen5853" type="x-p"/>

                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XXV.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p n="1">1 MOreover, David and the captains of the host <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Both of the Civil and Sacred Host: to wit, <ns0:hi>all the Princes of Israel, with the Priests and the Levites,</ns0:hi> whom David <ns0:hi>gathered together,</ns0:hi> ch<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 23. 2. for this very end that in their Presence and with their Approbation and Consent all these things might be esta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />blished; who are here fitly called <ns0:hi>the Captains of the Host;</ns0:hi> for the Princes were, under <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> the Chief Captains or Comman<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ders of the Militia or Trained Bands of the Kingdom; and as the Levites are called an <ns0:hi>Host,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>the Lords Host, Numb.</ns0:hi> 4. 23. and, elsewhere because of their Number and Order in Holy Ministrati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons; so these Priests and Levites were the Captains and Gover<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nours of the rest.</ns0:note> separated <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Distributed them into their several Ranks and Orders: Which, though chiefly done by <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> as a Prophet, and by Divine Direction, as hath been oft observed, yet is here imputed in part to the Captains of the Host, because it was done with their Concurrence and Approbation.</ns0:note> to the service of the sons of <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ch. 6. 33, 39. 2 Chr. 29. 30.</ns0:note> Asaph, and of <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">ver. 5.</ns0:note> Heman, and of <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Chr<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 35. 15.</ns0:note> Je<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duthun <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> To the Service of God under the Conduct and Command of these Persons.</ns0:note>, who should prophecy <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Praise God by singing the Psalms of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> (of which see on <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 16. 7.) and other sacred Songs made by themselves, who were Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets in some sort, or by other Prophets or Holy Men of God. Or this Action of theirs is called <ns0:hi>prophecying,</ns0:hi> because it had been for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />merly performed by the Prophets and the Sons of the Prophets: of which see 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 10. 5. & 19. 20. 2 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 3. 15. 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 15. 19.</ns0:note> with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals; and the number of the workmen <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Of the Persons employed in this Sacred Work.</ns0:note>, according to their service, was;</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 Of the sons of Asaph; Zaccur, and Joseph, and Nethaniah, and <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Otherwise cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led Iesharelah,</ns0:hi> ver. 14.</ns0:note> Asarelah, the sons of Asaph under the hands of Asaph <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Under his Oversight and Direction.</ns0:note>, which prophesied <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
